senses.definition: (transitive) To fasten, to join to (literally and figuratively).
examples: You need to attach the carabiner to your harness.
An officer is attached to a certain regiment, company, or ship.

quotes.text: [T]he ſhoulder-blade has no bony communication with the trunk, either by a joint, or proceſs, or in any other way. […] It is bedded in the fleſh; attached only to the muſcles.
quotes.reference: 1802, William Paley, “Of Mechanical Arrangement in the Human Frame”, in Natural Theology: Or, Evidences of the Existence and Attributes of the Deity, Collected from the Appearances of Nature, London: […] [F]or R[obert] Faulder, […], by Wilks and Taylor, […], →OCLC, page 117:

quotes.text: A huge stone, to which the cable on the left bank was attached, was removed years later
quotes.reference: 1849–1861, Thomas Babington Macaulay, The History of England from the Accession of James the Second, volume (please specify |volume=I to V), London: Longman, Brown, Green, and Longmans, →OCLC:

quotes.text: Turbines have been around for a long time—windmills and water wheels are early examples. The name comes from the Latin turbo, meaning vortex, and thus the defining property of a turbine is that a fluid or gas turns the blades of a rotor, which is attached to a shaft that can perform useful work.
quotes.reference: 2013 July-August, Lee S. Langston, “The Adaptable Gas Turbine”, in American Scientist:

quotes.text: The great interest which attaches to the mere knowledge of these facts cannot be doubted.

senses.definition: To include an attachment with a communication (especially an email or other electronic communication).
examples: I've attached the contract to this email.

senses.definition: To come into legal operation in connection with anything; to vest.

quotes.text: it therefore becomes important to know at what time the lien for taxes will attach.
quotes.reference: 1886, Thomas M. Cooley, A Treatise on the Law of Taxation:

senses.definition: To win the heart of; to connect by ties of love or self-interest; to attract; to fasten or bind by moral influence; with to.
examples: attached to a friend; attaching others to us by wealth or flattery

quotes.text: incapable of attaching a sensible man

quotes.text: God […] by various ties attaches man to man.

senses.definition: To connect, in a figurative sense; to ascribe or attribute; to affix; with to.
examples: to attach great importance to a particular circumstance
Some of the guilt must attach to the parents.

quotes.text: To this treasure a curse is attached.
